speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you are experiencing double vision, difficulty climbing stairs, and weakness in your arms. To understand the nature of these symptoms, how long have you been experiencing them, and did they start suddenly or gradually?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The fluctuating nature of your symptoms, worsening with activity and improving with rest, strongly suggests a neuromuscular junction issue. Does this pattern of weakness also affect your facial muscles, such as closing your eyes tightly or smiling?

REQUEST TEST: Acetylcholine_Receptor_Antibodies

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis

The presence of elevated Acetylcholine Receptor Antibodies, combined with your classic symptoms of fluctuating weakness that worsens with activity (ptosis/diplopia on looking up/down, limb weakness) and improves with rest, confirms the diagnosis of Myasthenia Gravis. Given your specific complaint of difficulty climbing stairs, we must also assess for bulbar or respiratory muscle involvement. Do you experience any shortness of breath, trouble swallowing, or choking on liquids?
